identity.title: Two Effects, One Trigger: On the Modality Gap, Object Bias, and Information Imbalance in Contrastive Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: The paper analyzes the modality gap and object bias in contrastive vision-language models and investigates why both emerge.

contributions.claim: It evaluates how the modality gap relates to performance and embedding-space organization.
It introduces a definition and corresponding measure of object bias.
It identifies information imbalance between images and captions as the reported driver of both phenomena and connects the modality gap with logit entropy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their object-bias analysis by introducing an explicit definition and measure for clean study.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the modality gap’s influence is usually outweighed by other factors, while closing the gap shows indications of improving performance.
They report that only a few embedding dimensions drive the gap and that image and text embedding spaces are organized differently.
Using controlled shared-information experiments, they report that information imbalance drives both the modality gap and object bias, with a connection to logit entropy.

narrative_sequence.summary: VLMs perform well on zero-shot object recognition but poorly on attribute recognition; prior work links this contrast to the modality gap and object bias.
The authors analyze the modality gap, reporting limited typical influence but indications of improvement when it is closed, plus sparse and differently organized embedding dimensions.
They define and measure object bias, finding that it does not inherently worsen performance on attributes or other concepts.
Controlled experiments varying shared image-caption information identify information imbalance as the reported common driver and link the gap to logit entropy.

source_observation.claim: The paper separates the analysis of two related phenomena by introducing a specific object-bias measure, then uses controlled variation of shared information to investigate their common cause.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research pattern is to operationalize a disputed concept before testing mechanisms that may unify multiple effects.
lessons.application: For a paper studying several correlated representation pathologies, define measurable constructs first and vary a shared candidate factor experimentally.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when the construct cannot be operationalized without imposing the very mechanism under investigation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated VLMs, datasets, procedures for closing the gap or controlling shared information, or quantitative effect sizes.
The reported indications and connections do not establish the magnitude, generality, or causal validity of the findings from the abstract alone.
